item.title: 25 November 2026: Accepted risks, Output for automation, Drupal core installer, NoisyTCP
item.description:
Added

  • Accessibility, to WCAG 2.2 AA: the documentation (both sites, every page, light and dark) and the HTML reports pass every automated WCAG 2.0, 2.1 and 2.2 A and AA check; contrast was raised where it fell short, links in text are underlined, targets are at least 24 by 24 pixels, keyboard focus is always visible, pages reflow at 320 pixels wide, and motion stops for those who ask. The PDF reports are tagged (PDF/UA): headings, paragraphs, tables with header cells, and links in reading order, decoration marked as artifacts, with their language and title. Every tool honors NO_COLOR, for screen readers in a terminal.

  • Accepted risks: ACCEPT_FILE in psf.conf, or psf-report --accept FILE, names a list of accepted findings (ignore: cves: with a reason, exclude: paths: by plain substring). Their findings are listed in an Accepted section of every report with the reason, are not counted, raise no alert and do not trip --fail-on; a finding of kind compromise is never accepted. Other sections of the file are not read, so a repository's .aikido file serves as it is. As root the list must be root's; a list that cannot be read never stops a run.

  • Records carry their time three ways, from one reading of the clock: ts to the second, unchanged; a new ts_ms to the millisecond (2026-11-26T06:00:00.412Z), which the ECS output uses for @timestamp; and a new ts_epoch_ms, the same instant as an integer. The reports, psf-status and psf-run read times leniently (any offset or fraction, or epoch values) and order runs by the most precise time a record carries, so two runs in the same second are told apart; a same-day rerun's file name uses UTC, as the day folders do.

  • The changelog as a feed: https://privacysafe.app/docs/security-patches/changelog.xml (RSS 2.0), one item for each day of changes, each carrying that day's entries with absolute links; the changelog page shows the address and every page names the feed.

  • Output for automation for every check: all 83 bash tools write records with --output jsonl and honor read-only mode; 77 tools changed for it, each one minor version up. Every read-only command of every tool (133) was run in jsonl mode and gave valid records ending in one verdict whose exit matches the run's, and every command that changes a host (90) was refused in read-only mode. psf-run with TOOLS = auto runs 77 of them; a tool says how to run it in a # psf-run: line near its top (audit for the rsyslog audit, none for the PHP session audit, manual (reason) for the six that need a site's address, server or module names, or macOS), and show-config lists the manual ones with their reason. php2shell-watch.sh, which follows logs live, and the two PowerShell tools do not write records.

  • Elastic Common Schema: psf-report --format ecs, or ecs in FORMATS for psf-run, writes the records with ECS field names (@timestamp, host.name, event.provider, event.action, event.code, event.sequence, log.level, message, vulnerability.id, file.path, and event.reference for the fix link), with every other field under psf, as records.ecs.ndjson.

  • Drupal core installer (CVE-2026-132165, SA-CORE-2026-017, and CVE-2026-136716, SA-CORE-2026-019): drupal-installer-check.sh 1.0.0. Anyone can use core/install.php to reinstall a running Drupal site under conditions Drupal does not publish: a takeover or code execution. Both advisories are rated Highly critical and are exploited; CVE-2026-132165 is on CISA's KEV list since 24 November. SA-CORE-2026-019 (25 November) found sites in an incomplete install state still open after the first fix; its affected range ends before 10.6.23, 11.3.23 and 11.4.14, and update.php must run after updating. Drupal says a site that has secured its installer is not vulnerable. check judges each site's core against both advisories and reports whether the installer is there, any rule naming it, and whether the web server's account can change settings.php; --url tests the live installer; hunt reads the access logs for installer requests and looks for PHP under sites/*/files and a recently changed settings.php; mitigate blocks the installer with a 403 in Apache (one configuration file for every site) and nginx (a snippet included in each Drupal server block), because a core update or composer install restores a removed core/install.php; each edited file is backed up, the change is tested with apachectl -t or nginx -t and taken back if the test fails, and only then reloaded. --remove also moves the installer into a backup it checks by SHA-256 (a file Drupal ships is never deleted). It tightens settings.php. rollback takes it all back, and never overwrites a configuration file changed since or an installer a core update has restored. It writes --output jsonl from the start.

  • NoisyTCP (CVE-2026-99288, and CVE-2026-99676): linux-kernel-noisytcp-check.sh 1.0.0. A race in TCP's lockless established lookup lets anyone who can reach a TCP port crash the host, no login needed, when packets are spread across CPUs (two or more receive queues, or RPS). Every kernel from 4.4 is affected; fixed upstream in 5.10.275, 5.15.226, 6.1.193, 6.6.163, 6.12.117, 6.18.63 and 7.3.4, and by Debian 12 (6.1.192-1), Debian 13 (6.12.117-1) and RHEL 8.8, 8.10, 9.9 and 10.3 (Red Hat advisories of 23 and 24 November); Ubuntu had fixes in progress only. The sibling restores memory ordering on weakly ordered processors (Arm, POWER, RISC-V): fixed only in 6.12.118, 6.18.64 and 7.3.5, so a 5.10 to 6.6 kernel fixed for NoisyTCP is not fixed for it there; on x86 it does not apply. check judges both by the kernel's origin (stable series, Debian, the RHEL update stream, Ubuntu's main kernel, a vendor changelog) and reports the exposure (SYN cookies, receive queues, RPS and RFS, listeners, network namespaces); hunt looks for the crash in the kernel logs and notes crash dumps; mitigate turns SYN cookies off (--syncookies) or cuts an interface to one receive queue with RPS and RFS off (--single-queue IFACE), and rollback puts it back. It writes --output jsonl from the start. Every version was taken from the researcher's advisory, the kernel CVE records, Red Hat's advisories and the Debian and Ubuntu trackers; a summary that circulated on 24 November called RHEL 9.8 and 10.2 kernels and Ubuntu 24.04 6.8.0-151.151 safe, and none of them carries the fix.

  • Output for automation, the format: --output jsonl (or PSF_OUTPUT=jsonl) makes a script write JSON Lines, one self-describing record per line (a start record, sections, an event for each finding with its level, CVE IDs and, where the script tags it, kind, code, path and a link to what to do, any other line as text, and a verdict with the exit code, the counts and whether the tool found anything on the host to check). Without it a script prints exactly what it printed before. PSF_READ_ONLY=1 refuses every command that changes the host before it starts, by name and again at the lock every change takes. automation/psf-report.py turns the records of any number of runs and hosts into a short summary, a full plain-text report, Markdown, an HTML page or a PDF made with Python alone, lists what needs attention most serious first, and exits 1 on --fail-on crit or warn. The HTML page and the PDF carry the PrivacySafe logo and colors, privacysafe.app links and both contacts as mail links (help@privacysafe.net, and security@privacysafe.net for security issues); the PDF's metadata names PrivacySafe Security Patches and privacysafe.app. psf-status shows at a terminal what the newest records say, the way systemctl status shows a service: the status, when the checks last ran and whether the logs are stale, one line per tool, the findings most serious first and the earlier days; psf-run runs the checks every night from cron (psf-run --quiet) as one settings file, /etc/psf-security-patches/psf.conf, says: where the logs go (LOG_DIR), how long they stay (KEEP_DAYS), which reports to write beside the records (FORMATS: summary, text, Markdown, HTML, PDF), which checks (TOOLS, auto by default), when and how to alert (ALERT_ON, ALERT_COMMAND), a time limit per tool (TIMEOUT) and settings for the tools (ENV); psf-run show-config shows each value and where it came from, and psf-status and psf-logs read the same file. Security, found in this release's own new code before it shipped: psf-report --out wrote through a predictable temporary name that another account could point at a root file (it now writes a new, unguessable, private file and renames it); a line a tool printed, such as a crafted file name, could pass for a record (each run now marks its own records with a secret); a planted oversized file could exhaust a reader's memory (files over 256 MB, links, devices and pipes are now skipped); run as root, these programs now refuse code or settings another account could change, and say at a terminal why they use root; as root, a tool's capture file is made in /tmp whatever TMPDIR says, and it no longer outlives a killed run. psf-logs lists the log folder, removes the days past their retention (prune --keep-days N, 90 by default, which the daily check runs) and clears it (clear --yes), never following a link and writing every removal to syslog; the packages put psf-status, psf-report and psf-logs on the PATH as links in /usr/bin. The automation guide has a section for system administrators: which output for what, jq recipes, a daily check with its cron line, several hosts, a log platform, and what each part needs. automation/examples/ holds example records and reports in every format, with screenshots of two checks run in a terminal (the Drupal installer and NoisyTCP checks), of psf-status, psf-logs, psf-run and psf-report in a terminal, and of the HTML report (light and dark) and the PDF (shown in the READMEs and on the site), made from real runs on a test machine with its host names, paths and times replaced. Record text is treated as hostile: escaped everywhere, never made a link, and the HTML page runs under a content security policy that allows no script. Every record is numbered (seq), so run and seq identify it. The format follows, closely rather than exactly, the joint guide Best Practices for Event Logging and Threat Detection (2024), the NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 AU controls and OMB M-26-14; the guide says where it stops short. magento-check.sh, nginx-oct2026-check.sh, expat-check.sh and agentic-attack-check.sh have it in this release; the rest follow.

Changed

  • A check whose software is not on the host now says it does not apply and exits 0, as the rest of the collection does, instead of exit 2 (could not check), which psf-run would report as a failed tool every night: the MySQL client, Ghostscript, OpenSSH on musl, Apache Roller, Etherpad and EasyApache 4 PHP (check only; its mitigate still stops) checks. php2shell-cpanel-mitigate.sh stopped with exit 1 after FATAL; it exits 2, as every script does. php-session-audit.sh accepts --output. The KVM escape check takes its lock only for a change, not a dry run, and read-only mode refuses its changes.
  • psf-run starts each tool in the install folder rather than /: the GhostAction check scans the current folder by default and, from /, read the whole filesystem past the time limit.
  • optimizely-optimjack-check.sh 1.0.1 and its README: the OPTIMJACK compromise now has a CVE, CVE-2026-132224 (published 18 November; a flaw in Optimizely Web Experimentation's account signup flow that let the attacker impersonate users and change Project JavaScript), on CISA's KEV list since 24 November. The Idunno.AntiCsrf README (CVE-2026-131914) records CISA's KEV listing of 24 November and its forensic-triage flag.
  • Red Hat advisories: refreshed to 25 November 2026 by merging Red Hat's exports of 1 October to 24 November and 11 to 25 November into the list of 1 April to 23 November (9,059 advisories; the newer export wins where both have one). 80 of the 217 CVEs now have an advisory, 726 in all. NoisyTCP's advisories (RHSA-2026:102167, 102168, 102218, 102219, and 102709 for RHEL 8.8) are in the data and the linux-kernel README's table and leave _known_outside_window; linux-kernel-noisytcp-check.sh knows the RHEL 8.8 fix. Ghostscript's CVE-2026-125396 has Red Hat advisories now and its README shows them. rhsa.py 1.0.2: the audit also reports a CVE a placed README names, with advisories, that its placement leaves out, so a tool added to a README with a block cannot go without its Red Hat section unnoticed; of the 29 such CVEs it found, the 22 that a folder's tool checks are now in their README's Red Hat section (nginx 10, PHP 4, Pillow 4, Next.js, Expat, Ruby, and CVE-2026-64564 on the kernel page, which the nginx page points to), and the other 6 are left out with a recorded reason: 4 PHP CVEs whose advisories all appear already, and 2 mentioned only in passing.
  • magento-check.sh 4.1.0, nginx-oct2026-check.sh 1.1.0, expat-check.sh 1.2.0 and agentic-attack-check.sh 2.1.0: structured output and read-only mode. Magento's findings name their kind (a flawed release is a vulnerability, an open upload folder an exposure, a PHP file in it a compromise) and carry a stable code; Magento and nginx say when a host has nothing for them to check. agentic-attack-check.sh no longer prints Permission denied for a process environment it may not read.

item.title: 23 November 2026: Magento, Adobe Commerce and Mage-OS, AI-driven attack frameworks, VMware vCenter directory service, N-central Legacy API and Apache Axis and 6 more
item.description:
Security

  • Five scripts ran, as root, a program they had found in a folder another account could write, so a user who planted node under ~/.nvm, or an application account that owns an /opt folder, could have had their code run as root during a check. Each now runs such a program as its owner, and as root only when root owns it and every folder above it (run_found): brotli-oct2026-check.sh 1.3.2 (node --version), emudhra-mitigate.sh 1.1.1 (node --version and Node.js's bundled roots), curl-oct2026-check.sh 1.0.2 (curl under /opt), ghostscript-upload2shell-check.sh 1.5.2 (gs under /opt) and expat-check.sh 1.1.1 (Python interpreters on PATH). Found while checking the new tools for the class of bug behind the symlink report. The new rf suite plants such programs and fails if one runs as root; it fails against the previous versions.

Changed

  • Red Hat advisories (no new CVE): refreshed from Red Hat's list for 1 April to 23 November 2026 (8,833 advisories). 78 of the 212 CVEs now have an advisory, 663 advisories in all (was 37 CVEs and 396 advisories to 3 November), and 25 tool READMEs show them. New sections for Next.js, Django, Jupyter, Java4Shell, Expat, APT and Apache HTTP/2, each with a note where the advisories are for products that bundle the code rather than the package itself.
  • rhsa.py 1.0.1: fetch and find --live read the CSAF index of Red Hat's Security Data API (csaf.json). Red Hat retired the CVRF index (cvrf.json) that 1.0.0 used, which now answers 404, so fetch could not download a list. They now ask for an uncompressed answer and decompress a gzip one, accept the CVE list under the names the index may use, when the index names no CVEs ask cve.json?advisory= for each advisory, as Red Hat's example script does, and stop only if that names none either, and on a 404 from the old address name the new one. Container images written without a registry (cryostat/…) keep their namespace, and CSAF product trees are read for CoreOS builds and kernel live patches as well. New: fetch --by-cve, which builds the list CVE by CVE from Red Hat's CVE records and each advisory's CSAF document, for the CVEs the READMEs and the placement table name. The index and the README sections built from it are unchanged.
  • README.md and packaging/README.md: the install commands and the examples name this release's files (26.11.26-1.0.0); they still named 26.11.20-1.0.0.
  • Next.js: nextjs-server-actions-check.sh 1.3.0 also judges every install against the November 2026 security release (3 November, 15.5.29 and 16.4.5), which fixes seven flaws: CVE-2026-119790 (cache disclosure across root params, rated high by Next.js), CVE-2026-119351, CVE-2026-119349, CVE-2026-119350, CVE-2026-119348 (cross-client response injection behind a pipelining proxy), CVE-2026-119346 (HttpOnly cookie values in an Edge header) and CVE-2026-119347 (SVG rejection bypass). A version before the release in its line is reported with the CVEs whose ranges cover it (CVE-2026-119350 from 16.4.0, as Netlify and the advisory list it) and exits 1, with or without Server Actions. A lockfile that pins Netlify's adapter @netlify/plugin-nextjs before 5.16.6 is reported too: on Netlify, cookies set in Middleware stay exposed (CVE-2026-119346) until that adapter release, whatever the Next.js version. For 16.x projects it reads next.config.* (or a build's .next/required-server-files.json) and source files to say whether Cache Components is on (the default for new projects since 16.4), how many files use 'use cache', whether Partial Prefetching is on, and whether a cacheHandler store keeps entries that must be purged after the upgrade or the default in-memory cache only needs a restart; 13.x and 14.x get no November fix and move to 15.5.29 or 16.4.5. The upgrade advice now names 15.5.29 and 16.4.5. Corrected: the README and the script had listed CVE-2026-119347 among the image optimizer flaws closed by 15.5.28 and 16.4.1; it is the November SVG bypass, fixed in 15.5.29 and 16.4.5. It now names, for each version that still carries them, the critical flaws of the earlier releases: GHSA-673q-mjm6-r5xr (14 October, unauthenticated code execution through use cache functions returning typed arrays, 16.0.0 to 16.4.0, no CVE; React upstream CVE-2026-126187), CVE-2026-96889 (14 October, SVG code execution through the librsvg inside sharp, 10.0.0 to 15.5.27 and 16.0.0 to 16.4.0), CVE-2026-75604 (25 August, path traversal to code execution on Windows filesystems only, reported as information) and the August AVIF flaw GHSA-2xp9-vwfh-vxw4. An app with no Server Action had been told it was "not exposed" for CVE-2026-94482 although the same release fixes two critical flaws that need none; the message now says so. New sharp check: every sharp version in each Next.js project's lockfiles and node_modules (regular files only, links not followed) is judged against CVE-2026-114111 (librsvg, before 0.35.5), CVE-2026-114112 (libheif, before 0.35.4) and CVE-2026-114113 (libvips, before 0.35.0), exit 1, because an upgraded Next.js still runs whatever sharp a lockfile or an override holds; images.dangerouslyAllowSVG is read from the config. Corrected: CVE-2026-114111 had been listed as a Next.js image optimizer flaw; it is the sharp package's record for the librsvg defect behind CVE-2026-96889. New suite nxj.

Fixed

  • READMEs: 50 commented download lines (curl -fLO "$BASE/...") still named the old folders after the move; they now use the category paths.
  • Packages: the php2shell-watch systemd unit the .deb and .rpm install now runs the installed script, /opt/psf-security-patches/runtimes/php/php2shell-watch.sh, as the README says; it named /usr/local/sbin/php2shell-watch.sh, which the packages do not install. The .rpm recipe also had the old path to the unit file and did not build after the move.

Added

  • Documentation site: packaging/site-redirects.tsv lists the 59 pages that moved into category folders, and gen-site.py --theme privacysafe-app leaves a forwarding page at each old address (meta refresh, noindex, the new page as canonical, not in the sitemap), so links published before the move keep working. check-site.py checks each forwarding page: its target exists and is not itself a forwarding page, the canonical names the target, and noindex is set. A map entry that would overwrite a page, or point to one the build did not write, stops the build.
  • Magento, Adobe Commerce and Mage-OS: magento-check.sh 4.0.0 adds three exploited flaws to BlockStrap (CVE-2026-103849): PolyShell (CVE-2026-48356, unauthenticated upload through the guest cart, CISA KEV 27 October), CVE-2026-71362 (customer account takeover, CISA KEV 24 September) and StyleSmuggler (CVE-2026-75650, CVSS 10.0, CISA KEV 8 September). Each flaw is judged on its own: a dated release or a Mage-OS release gives a firm answer, and StyleSmuggler needs evidence of hotfix VULN-39341, which no release carries (the October one included), so a store on -2026-oct without it is now reported, where 3.0.1 reported it fixed. check also reads whether the PolyShell upload folder is closed (nginx locations and their order, the Apache .htaccess) and counts files in it. New hunt (store files, host implants, cron, known hashes, command-server connections, access and exception logs; read-only SQL printed for the database), mitigate (the upload-folder .htaccess, written as the folder's owner without following links, and an nginx guard snippet that nothing includes until you do) and rollback.
  • AI-driven attack frameworks: new read-only agentic-attack-check.sh for GNU/Linux hosts, covering ARTEX (FBI FLASH-20261113-001), CAIRN, CyberStrikeAI, HexStrike AI, PentAGI, Strix, Hermes, RedAmon, Xalgorix, PentestSwarm and Agent Zero, driven by a list of 644 indicators with a confidence each (indicators.tsv; most from ThreatDefence's MIT-licensed list, whose notice it keeps, plus Wiz's addresses and a survey of exposed consoles). check finds the frameworks' images and containers (including the backdoored ARTEX images on Docker Hub), consoles on this host's ports by page text or favicon hash, processes by command line or environment variable names, framework files and folders, files with a published SHA-256 or MD5, AI clients wired to an offensive MCP server, and the weaknesses the agents use (source maps in web folders, MySQL logs written into a web folder with relative paths resolved against the data directory, an empty secure_file_priv). hunt reads access logs (user agents, probe requests, headers, markers, source addresses), the auth log, syslog and the journal (addresses, domains), web folders, histories, cron and units, and current processes and connections. export prints addresses, domains, user agents, hashes, images or strings for other tools. High-confidence matches are findings, medium ones leads, low ones only counted. It never follows a link and leaves itself and its list out of every search.
  • Repository layout: the 69 tool folders now sit in six category folders, servers/, system/, runtimes/, web-apps/, developer/ and threats/, beside packaging/ and docs/: eight top-level folders instead of 71. Every README link, raw download URL, manual page, site page, Red Hat cross-reference and test path was moved with them, and the packages install the same tree under /opt/psf-security-patches/. Tool pages on the documentation site move with their folders (for example servers/nginx/).
  • VMware vCenter directory service: new vcenter-dirsvc-check.sh for CVE-2026-123890 (CVSS 9.8, VMSA-2026-0009, exploited since September, CISA KEV 20 November). check HOST... asks each vCenter for its build with the unauthenticated call every vSphere client makes first and judges it against 9.1.1.0200 (build 25901347), 9.0.2.0200 (25901331) and 8.0 U3m (25934264), and says whether this machine reaches port 2012; on the appliance it reads vpxd -v. hunt looks for Mandiant's file indicators and SSO user changes; mitigate on the appliance lets only ALLOW_FROM reach port 2012 (and 443 if asked) with its own iptables chain, with --dry-run and rollback.
  • N-central Legacy API and Apache Axis: new ncentral-legacyapi-check.sh for CVE-2026-90436 ("4EverAble2Shell", exploited, CISA KEV 18 November): asks each N-central server whether its Legacy API answers, finds Apache Axis 1.x jars (no fixed release exists) on the host, in Java class paths and in containers, and hunts for the xvd.service miner, its folders, the attackers' address and the jline gadget in web logs.
  • Java4Shell: new java4shell-check.sh for CVE-2026-114938: reads the CPU's AVX-512 VBMI flag and judges every Java runtime (including bundled ones, and those in containers through /proc/PID/root) by its release file without running it, a distribution package also by its changelog, and every running JVM for the -XX:-UseBASE64Intrinsics flag. mitigate adds that flag to running systemd services through a drop-in, with rollback.
  • pam-mysql: new pam-mysql-check.sh for CVE-2026-124749: the PAM services that use it, sshd's PermitEmptyPasswords, the package against Debian's fixed versions, and with QUERY_DB=1 the rows with no password (pam-mysql's own read credentials, passed through the environment); hunt marks password logins by those accounts.
  • iTerm2 on macOS: new iterm2-kitty-check.sh for the iTerm2 3.6.1 to 3.7.8 terminal-reply command execution (no CVE; fixed in 3.7.9): finds every copy and its version, says whether this macOS can run the fix, and scan finds files that carry the Kitty graphics escape sequence (macOS and GNU/Linux).
  • Idunno.AntiCsrf on Mono: new web-apps/aspnet/idunno-anticsrf-check.sh for GNU/Linux. Mono's System.Web loads a module registered under this name and its ObjectStateFormatter deserializes with no MAC, like the .NET Framework's. The tool finds Mono applications (mod_mono, .webapp files, nginx, running XSP and fastcgi-mono-server), the DLL, registrations, the machine-wide web.config, the GAC and Mono's shadow copies; hunt reads error and access logs; mitigate never writes through a symbolic link (no-follow reads, a new file renamed over the original with its owner and mode), with rollback. The PowerShell tool gained IIS shared configuration, IIS Express, application pools, ASP.NET shadow copies, events 1309 and 4688, shells under w3wp.exe, and the same refusal to follow links.
  • binary-parser: new binary-parser-check.sh for CVE-2026-134814 (CVSS 4.0 9.2, every release before 2.3.1; NVD published 22 November) and CVE-2026-1245 ("ParserPoison", every release before 2.3.0). An application that builds a binary-parser definition from data it does not control runs that data as JavaScript when the parser compiles. check reads package.json files, every lockfile format, nested and Debian/Ubuntu-packaged copies and bundled copies, and judges each by its version and by the error strings each fix added to the code, so a copy patched in place reads as fixed and a bundle with no package.json is still judged. audit DIR lists the source lines that pass a non-literal value as a name, an encoding, one of the affected options or a namely() alias. Read-only.
  • Idunno.AntiCsrf on IIS: new web-apps/aspnet/idunno-anticsrf-check.ps1, the collection's second PowerShell tool, for CVE-2026-131914 (CVSS 4.0 9.3, exploited, Mandiant MNDT-2026-0048): a defunct ASP.NET WebForms anti-CSRF module (last released in 2008, no fix) that passes the CSRF form field to an unkeyed ObjectStateFormatter on every POST, so one anonymous request runs code as w3wp.exe. check reads applicationHost.config for every site and finds the DLL by name, by Mandiant's three hashes and by its assembly name, every Web.config that registers the module (classic, integrated, inside <location>, machine-wide) and the GAC; hunt reads the IIS W3C logs for large POSTs to .aspx pages answered 302 or 500 and lists recently changed site files; mitigate removes the registrations with a copy of each file, an XML read-back and restore on failure, -DryRun and a lock; rollback puts the files back byte for byte. Runs under Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7, including on GNU/Linux against shares and backups.

Changed

  • OpenSSH musl password bypass: the README table row names CVE-2026-123158.
  • The documentation site's and the manual pages' "Newest" lists cover 2 to 23 November.
  • Node.js October 2026 tool: the README records CISA's listing of CVE-2026-111497 (27 October 2026, due 10 November) and names the three other high CVEs the same releases fix (CVE-2026-105482, CVE-2026-105483, CVE-2026-106069), which the version check covers and the Brotli guard does not.
  • Next.js: GHSA-673q-mjm6-r5xr is given as 9.5 under CVSS 4.0 (Next.js) and 10 under CVSS 3.1 (GitLab).
  • README.md, packaging/gen-site.py, packaging/gen-docs.py: every new tool registered; the count line reads 84 scripts, 212 CVEs, 85 projects, 11 programming languages and 9 other global security incidents.
  • docs/: regenerated (212 CVEs, 82 manual pages, 69 tool pages).

item.title: 22 November 2026: Apache Roller XML-RPC deserialization, Ghostscript Upload2Shell
item.description:
Added

  • Apache Roller XML-RPC deserialization: new apache-roller-xmlrpc-check.sh for CVE-2026-129448 / CVE-2026-82384, a critical (CVSS 9.8) unauthenticated deserialization RCE in Apache Roller 4.0.0 to 6.1.5, actively exploited and in CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. Roller's XML-RPC servlet ships with the underlying library's enabledForExtensions option set to true, so it deserializes a non-standard vendor value type carrying a base64-encoded Java-serialized object before any authentication check runs; Roller's own admin-UI toggle for XML-RPC does not gate this on an unpatched install, since the deserialization happens before that setting is ever read. Fixed in Roller 6.1.6, which disables the vendor extension types and adds a new filter that finally makes the toggle work. check finds every Tomcat instance this host has the same way tomcat-oct2026-check.sh does (explicit CATALINA_HOME/CATALINA_BASE, running processes' -Dcatalina.home=/-Dcatalina.base=, then filesystem fallback) and detects a patched install via the presence of the post-fix XmlRpcEnabledFilter, since a deployed WAR does not reliably carry its own version number on disk. hunt greps access logs for POST /roller-services/xmlrpc. mitigate applies either of Apache's two named workarounds: enabledForExtensions=false by default (no real cost, since it only disables the dangerous vendor extension type), or --remove-mapping to comment out the servlet mapping entirely (a real cost, since it also disables the legitimate Blogger/MetaWeblog API, so this option is gated behind confirmed exposure unless --force is given). --dry-run previews either change; --restart restarts a detected Tomcat unit. rollback (with its own --dry-run) restores. Version 1.7.0.
  • Ghostscript Upload2Shell: new ghostscript-upload2shell-check.sh for CVE-2026-125396, a -dSAFER sandbox escape via a crafted Type 1 font in the .putgstringcopy procedure, reached through ImageMagick, Pillow, WordPress, Roundcube, CUPS and more by file content rather than name or extension; fixed in Ghostscript 10.08.0. check cross-references installed packages against each distribution's own fixed-build list and flags a real trap: Ghostscript's own 10.08.0 release candidate, built before the fix commit, reports the identical version string as the real release, so an exact match with no owning package is reported as undetermined rather than clean. It also audits ImageMagick's policy.xml for whether the coders mitigate would block are already blocked. mitigate adds the long-standing community-documented policy.xml lines blocking the PS/PS2/PS3/EPS/XPS coders (--include-pdf also blocks PDF), gated behind confirmed exposure (--force to override) since blocking these coders has a real cost to legitimate PostScript/EPS/XPS processing; --dry-run previews regardless of exposure. rollback (with --dry-run) restores. rules covers what mitigate cannot automate: the Pillow formats= argument, WordPress's and Roundcube's separate upload-path fixes (the Roundcube one already checked by this collection's own roundcube-oct2026-check.sh), and print-queue authentication. Version 1.5.0.

Security

  • Linux kernel: linux-kernel-kvm-escape-check.sh 1.0.1 fixes a link-following race (CWE-59, CWE-377) in mitigate --unload, reported privately by an outside researcher. Version 1.0.0 sent modprobe's error output, as root, to /tmp/psf-kvm-rm.PID and /tmp/psf-kvm-ins.PID. The process id is visible to every local user, so an unprivileged user could place a symlink at that path first and have the root run truncate and overwrite any file root can write (/etc/shadow, a cron file, a systemd unit) with modprobe's message. It does not raise privileges or disclose data; it is an integrity and availability flaw, rated Low (CVSS 4.0 about 3.7). The output is now captured in a variable, so nothing is written under /tmp. Only mitigate --unload on a multi-user host was affected; check, rules, rollback and mitigate without --unload never reached that code.
  • A sweep of every script for the same pattern found two more and closed them the same way: apache-mod-http2-check.sh 1.1.1 (the running module list read by check, and the apachectl -t output in mitigate, both went through a PID-based /tmp file) and etherpad-static-traversal-check.sh 1.1.1 (the nginx -t output in mitigate). The Etherpad tool also now removes its one mktemp file on exit, like the rest of the collection.
  • claude-code-vsx-oct2026-check.sh 1.3.2: clean, run by a user with no HOME set and no BACKUP_ROOT, fell back to a fixed folder under /tmp for the files it moves aside, which another user could create first. It now stops and asks for BACKUP_ROOT, and refuses a backup folder it does not own.

Fixed

  • An install whose version could not be read or parsed, or that is older than the range one CVE covers, no longer counts as clean. 21 scripts printed a warning (or a green line saying "far out of date, update anyway") and then exited 0. They now exit 1 for these cases, and each README's exit codes say so: pillow-oct2026-check.sh, grav-core-check.sh, grav-login-check.sh, nextjs-server-actions-check.sh, couchdb-check.sh, expat-check.sh, drf-check.sh, jupyter-check.sh, laravel-tokenguard-check.sh, haproxy-check.sh (also a 3.5 development build), bind-check.sh, trafficserver-check.sh, drupal-core-check.sh, sagemaker-check.sh (installed copies and pins), roundcube-oct2026-check.sh, storybook-check.sh, sentry-nextjs-check.sh, wordpress-pt-check.sh, litellm-escalation-check.sh, gitea-check.sh and craftcms-check.sh (also an end-of-life major version). Where the vendor states the release that introduced a flaw (HAProxy before 3.1, YOOtheme before 5, the per-CVE ranges of baserCMS and GitLab), an older release is still reported as outside that flaw, with no change.
  • apache-mod-http2-check.sh: --help now documents mitigate --dry-run, which the code already accepted.
  • Linux kernel module blocker: the README now lists the kvm_amd row of the exploited group (CVE-2026-99312) that linux-kernel-module-block.sh 1.1.0 added on 20 November, and gives the right total, 43 rows.
  • CHANGELOG.md: the two entries each for 19 and 20 November are merged into one per day.
  • Pillow: pillow-oct2026-check.sh 1.1.0 no longer treats a copy older than 2.6.0 as outside the problem. Pillow 13.0.0 fixed far more than the two CVEs the tool names, and Ubuntu's USN-9064-1 (12 November) lists releases back to 2.3.0 as affected by heap writes that can run code (CVE-2026-112393, CVE-2026-112398, CVE-2026-112403). Every copy older than 13.0.0 is now reported with them, and a package changelog naming any of them counts as a backport. The README has the fixed python3-pil versions for every Ubuntu release down to 14.04 (Ubuntu Pro) and the USN-9064-2 regression fix of 16 November.
  • Expat: the fix for CVE-2026-115506 shipped on 2 November as Expat 2.10.0, not as the planned 2.9.1, together with CVE-2026-113351, CVE-2026-117610 and CVE-2026-118370. expat-check.sh 1.1.0 now treats 2.10.0 as the fixed release and accepts any of the four in a package changelog. Debian's tracker still listed every Debian release as vulnerable in November; Alpine ships 2.10.0-r0.
  • Next.js: nextjs-server-actions-check.sh 1.1.0 and the README say that the same fixed releases (15.5.28 and 16.4.1) close three image optimizer flaws that need no Server Action (CVE-2026-96889, CVE-2026-114111, CVE-2026-119347; one also needs sharp 0.35.5) and that 16.4.1 carries the React Server Components fix for CVE-2026-126187.
  • OpenSSL: notes CVE-2026-121481 (Base64 encoding of an exceptionally large input), whose fixed releases 4.0.4 and 4.1.1 were scheduled for 1 December; the tool does not check for it until a fixed release exists. Brotli: notes that CISA added CVE-2026-111497 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 27 October. vsftpd: notes CVE-2026-119567 (denied commands still run through their X-prefixed aliases, rated Low) and Red Hat's cmds_denied workaround; CVE-2026-119568 still had no upstream fix in November.
  • Regression suites: cv, gs and p2s no longer depend on the build machine (a missing ss, a missing Ghostscript) or expect the pre-19 November cleanup behavior of php2shell-mitigate.sh.
  • Conventions across the collection: every script that changes the host now takes the shared lock (apache-roller-xmlrpc-check.sh 1.7.1, ghostscript-upload2shell-check.sh 1.5.1, apache-mod-http2-check.sh 1.2.0, etherpad-static-traversal-check.sh 1.2.0 and mysql-client-check.sh 1.3.0 did not), and every such command has --dry-run (Etherpad mitigate and rollback, MySQL harden and rollback, Apache rollback). The rollback of the Apache, Etherpad and MySQL tools now reports a file it could not restore, which a pipeline used to hide. The Roller and Ghostscript tools print a plain version line and a closing Verdict like the rest, and their READMEs gained the quick start and command table they lacked. Five scripts gained the Assisted-by line they were missing, and sixteen that carried two model names keep one. READMEs that showed a host-changing command without sudo now show it, and first-person and testing narrative is gone from the READMEs.
  • nginx2root: the Linux SCTP flaw Xint chained with CVE-2026-123007 now has an id, CVE-2026-64564 (Red Hat CVSS 3.1 7.8). nginx2root-check.sh 1.1.1 and the README name it and say its fix is in mainline (19 November) but in no stable kernel as of 22 November; the module blocker README notes that blocking sctp removes its surface.

Changed

  • nginx2root-check.sh: documented all 10 CVEs the 18 November nginx releases fix, not only the 5 this script actively audits for, most notably CVE-2026-118899 (high, a TLS 1.3 worker-hang denial of service reachable on an ordinary TLS 1.3 server block with no special configuration); the version check already covered it correctly, this was a documentation gap. Version 1.0.0 to 1.1.0.
  • openssh-musl-check.sh: backfilled CVE-2026-123158 ("sshole"), assigned after this script was first written; corrected the severity to CVSS 8.1 High and added the CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities date. The detection logic, built around the underlying musl crypt() mechanism rather than a version string, needed no change. Version 1.0.0 to 1.0.1.
  • ruby-regexp-oct2026-check.sh: backfilled CVE-2026-132825, now assigned to GHSA-34m4-m9fh-gqp5, one of the seven November GHSAs this script already tracks, and updated vendor patch status (Mastodon, OpenProject and Discourse fixed; GitLab, GitHub Enterprise Server and Chatwoot not, as of 20 November). Version 2.0.0 to 2.0.1.
  • php-session-audit.sh: added a new audit step for CVE-2026-129291 (PHP-FPM worker-to-master privilege escalation via catch_workers_output), a different CVE from the same 19 November PHP release; runtimes/php/README.md documents four more previously-unmentioned CVEs from that release.
  • Apache Roller XML-RPC deserialization, Ghostscript Upload2Shell: both new tools went through seven completeness/overlap review passes against the rest of the collection before shipping, each finding and fixing something real. Against tomcat-oct2026-check.sh: Roller's Tomcat discovery was filesystem-glob only, missing a non-default install or a multi-instance CATALINA_BASE; fixed to also discover via running processes. Also fixed a comment-blind grep in Roller's exposure check, and pointed Ghostscript's Roundcube guidance at roundcube-oct2026-check.sh, which already checks the same version threshold. A collection-wide grep for --dry-run on mitigate found it in 28 other scripts and missing from these two; added to both. Against wordpress-wp2shell-check.sh: mitigations with a real functional cost should be gated behind confirmed exposure plus --force, and its rollback also supports --dry-run; added both patterns. Running this collection's own internal/tests/quality_audit.py.txt directly against both scripts found and fixed a temp-file-without-a-trap hygiene gap in both, and a real typo in Ghostscript's help text (IMAGEMACK_POLICY_FILES, missing "GI", naming a variable the script never actually reads). Running internal/tests/readonly_snapshot_test.py.txt found it had silently skipped testing hunt for both scripts, since their header used a heading its command parser does not recognize instead of this collection's own "Usage:" convention; fixed, and confirmed check and hunt are genuinely read-only for both. Writing the regression suites this collection's own tooling expects but neither script had (internal/tests/ar_test.sh.txt, internal/tests/gs_test.sh.txt, internal-only, shipped in the archive but not the published git repository) surfaced one more real issue: Roller's --restart used a fixed list of four candidate systemd unit names, unlike tomcat-oct2026-check.sh's own --restart, which discovers any tomcat*.service unit dynamically; fixed to match. Both suites now pass in full.
  • README.md, packaging/gen-site.py: added both new tools to the table and the site generator's category list; bumped the scripts/CVEs/projects count line (74 scripts, 189 CVEs, 77 projects).
  • docs/: regenerated (189 CVEs, 74 manual pages, 61 tool pages).

The CVEs set aside on 22 November as a poor fit (VMware vCenter, N-able N-central and Apache Axis, Java4Shell, pam-mysql and iTerm2) are covered as of 23 November; see above. The Next.js image and React Server Components flaws are documented in the Next.js README, and the OpenSSL base64 flaw in the OpenSSL README until its fix ships on 1 December.

item.title: 20 November 2026: Etherpad static path traversal, Linux kernel
item.description:
Added

  • Etherpad static path traversal: new etherpad-static-traversal-check.sh for CVE-2026-114516 / GHSA-mc8w-wjhw-45x5, a critical (CVSS 3.1 9.8) unauthenticated path traversal in Etherpad's /static/* handler. The route runs before Etherpad installs session and auth-check middleware, so no account or config setting gates it; a URL-encoded backslash (%5C) is the only separator that reaches a backslash-folding step added after the one sanitizer check meant to catch it, and the always-registered core plugin name gives every install a working prefix. A successful read reaches settings.json/credentials.json, environment-supplied secrets, TLS keys and the pad database; the disclosed admin password then mints an admin session, and the admin plugin installer gives remote code execution. Affects etherpad-lite 1.8.14 to 3.3.2; fixed in 3.3.3. check finds installed copies and reports their version; hunt greps logs for the plugin-static + encoded-backslash request signature; mitigate (nginx only) adds an http-level map plus a server-level if/return 400 to every HTTP-context server {} block found, explicitly skipping one nested in a mail {}/stream {} block, where nginx reuses the same keyword for something that doesn't support if/return; backs up, tests with nginx -t, rolls back on failure. rollback undoes it. Apache needs the equivalent RewriteCond added by hand (see the README). Version 1.1.0.
  • Linux kernel: linux-kernel-kvm-escape-check.sh for CVE-2026-99312, a KVM guest-to-host escape on AMD nested virtualization disclosed by Terra Security (Oren Yomtov) on 18 November 2026, demonstrated reading about 127 GB of host memory from a DigitalOcean droplet and writing to host kernel memory on a separate server the researchers controlled. check reports the kernel version against the fixed releases (6.12.118, 6.18.64, 7.3.5, mainline 7.4-rc2), whether the host is AMD, and kvm_amd's nested parameter; mitigate writes options kvm_amd nested=0 to modprobe.d and, with --unload, applies it now (every VM on the host must already be stopped). Kernel branches below 6.1 outside the two confirmed-affected ranges are reported unknown rather than clear, since the 2022 commit this flaw's precondition came from was widely backported at the time and other long-term branches are not ruled out. Version 1.0.0, 2026-11-20.
  • README.md, packaging/gen-site.py: added the new tool to the table; added etherpad to the site generator's category list; bumped the scripts/CVEs/projects count line (72 scripts, 152 CVEs, 75 projects).
  • docs/: regenerated (152 CVEs, 72 manual pages, 59 tool pages).

Changed

  • Apache mod_http2, Etherpad static path traversal, MySQL client programs: comparing these three newly-added tools against the collection's established mitigate-capable scripts (php2shell-mitigate.sh, php2shell-cpanel-mitigate.sh, wordpress-wp2shell-check.sh) surfaced two gaps all three shared. First, none checked for root before mitigate/harden/rollback, so running one as a non-root user failed with a raw permission-denied error from cp/sed/mkdir instead of a clear message; added the same need_root check the rest of the collection uses, verified with a real non-privileged test user. Second, apache-mod-http2-check.sh and etherpad-static-traversal-check.sh only ever told the person to reload the web server themselves; added a --reload option to both mitigate and rollback (graceful, via systemctl reload where that unit exists, otherwise apache2ctl -k graceful / nginx -s reload), matching wp2shell's existing --reload, and verified each one actually reloads a running server (starting it first if needed) and leaves the live result correct afterward. mysql-client-check.sh has no long-running daemon reading its config and so has no --reload to add; its README says why. Versions: apache-mod-http2-check.sh 1.0.0 to 1.1.0, mysql-client-check.sh 1.1.0 to 1.2.0, etherpad-static-traversal-check.sh 1.0.0 to 1.1.0 (folded into the entry above).
  • Linux kernel: linux-kernel-module-block.sh gained a kvm_amd row in its curated list (group exploited, CVE-2026-99312), pointing to the new linux-kernel-kvm-escape-check.sh mitigate rather than a full block, since blocking kvm_amd entirely stops all AMD virtualization, nested or not. Version 1.1.0.
  • packaging/build-release.sh and packaging/rpm/psf-security-patches.spec.in: fixed two reproducibility gaps found while verifying this release's own build. The .deb's DEBIAN/control and DEBIAN/md5sums are written after the mtime-normalization pass, so they carried the real build-time mtime into control.tar.xz's member timestamps, producing different compressed bytes on every build despite identical file content; they are now clamped to SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH explicitly before dpkg-deb runs. The .rpm's %license and %doc macros make rpm itself create their target directory and copy the named files into it as a packaging step that runs after %install, bypassing clamp_mtime_to_source_date_epoch for that directory entry; the files are now installed explicitly in %install (still tagged %license/%doc at their final path, so rpm -q --licensefiles/--docfiles are unaffected) and the whole buildroot is clamped explicitly once %install finishes. All three packages (.tar.gz, .deb, .rpm) were confirmed byte-identical across independent builds before this release shipped.

item.title: 19 November 2026: Apache mod_http2, MySQL client programs
item.description:
Added

  • Apache mod_http2: new apache-mod-http2-check.sh for CVE-2026-119618, a critical (CVSS 3.1 9.8) unauthenticated RCE in Apache HTTP Server's mod_http2, fixed in httpd 2.4.71 (released 11 November 2026) and found by Anthropic's OSS Scanner and Google Cloud's Vulnerability Research team. Affects httpd 2.4.55 to 2.4.70 with mod_http2 loaded and HTTP/2 (h2/h2c) turned on via a Protocols directive; the standalone mod_h2 project on GitHub (2.0.8 to 2.0.42) carries the same vulnerable code and was archived by its owner on 9 June 2026 with no fix. check reports version, module and Protocols state; hunt greps the error log for crash/corruption signatures; mitigate disables mod_http2 (resolving Debian/Ubuntu's conf-enabled/mods-enabled symlinks to the real file first, rather than silently replacing a symlink with a plain file), backs up, tests the config, and rolls back on failure. There is no configuration fix that keeps HTTP/2 usable; only upgrading or disabling it closes this. Version 1.0.0.
  • MySQL client programs: new mysql-client-check.sh for CVE-2026-114952, a critical (CVSS 3.1 9.1) unauthenticated flaw in MySQL's "Client programs" component (mysql, mysqldump, mysqlbinlog and others), published 17 November 2026 as part of Oracle's November 2026 CSPU. Oracle's advisory gives no technical root cause, as is its practice; this is a client-side issue, not a listening-server one, so there is no mitigate, only version detection and the behavioral guidance that follows from the vulnerability's shape (don't point client tools at a server you don't fully trust until upgraded). MySQL Server 8.0.x is not covered by Oracle's fix for this CVE at all, since 8.0 left Premier/CPU-eligible support in April 2026; check reports any 8.0.x client install as exposed with no confirmed remediation besides moving to 8.4 or later. harden adds one clearly-labeled, speculative exception for that 8.0 case: unconfirmed secondary analysis names the client's real, documented cleartext authentication plugin as a plausible mechanism, and harden can disable it as defense-in-depth, explicitly not a substitute for upgrading once a real patch exists. Version 1.1.0.

Changed

  • Ruby and GitLab Regexp/case conversion: ruby-regexp-oct2026-check.sh now also covers seven flaws Ruby fixed on 18 November 2026 in 4.0.10, 3.4.13 and 3.3.14, reported directly to Ruby rather than through GitLab, so none has a CVE yet (tracked by GHSA ID: GHSA-34m4-m9fh-gqp5, GHSA-7x2q-68qv-6p8x, GHSA-87fm-7w84-j2px, GHSA-wpqw-5qxg-m68r, GHSA-3p8q-wmhx-vm2w, GHSA-7whj-cfh7-xgm4, GHSA-pvgc-g7gj-pv6h). Five are further Onigmo regex-engine memory bugs; two are in String#upcase/downcase/capitalize/swapcase case conversion, a surface the October fixes didn't touch and one reached by code far more ordinary than compiling a user-supplied pattern. Three are critical, three high, one moderate, with working proof-of-concept RCE for six of the seven. check now reports, for every Ruby it finds, whether it's fixed for October only, for both, or for neither, since a build at exactly the October threshold (4.0.9, 3.4.12, 3.3.13) is still exposed to November. GitLab's embedded Ruby binary is now checked directly against the November thresholds rather than only through GitLab's own product-version table, since that table only ever tracked GitLab's own CVE-2026-110264 fix and no GitLab release bundles the November fix yet; the same direct check runs whether the embedded Ruby was found on disk or in a running process. scan is unchanged and still narrows down the regex-compilation half only; the case-conversion half has no comparable per-call-site signal, so check treats any Ruby below the new thresholds as exposed to it by default. Public tracking (https://verialabs.com/ruby2shell/) showed GitHub Enterprise Server, Mastodon, OpenProject and Chatwoot, which bundle Ruby the same way GitLab and Discourse do, also still unpatched as of 19 November; the script has no install detection for those four, and the README and script header now say so explicitly. Version 2.0.0.
  • PHP2Shell: php2shell-mitigate.sh and php-session-audit.sh now know the real fixed releases for CVE-2026-115560 (8.2.36, 8.3.37, 8.4.28, 8.5.13), shipped 19 November 2026 as part of a broader 18-CVE PHP release; the PATCHED_115560_X_Y table was empty before this since no fix existed yet. Both READMEs now also name CVE-2026-129289, a critical (CVSS 9.2) PHP-FPM request-smuggling RCE in the same release that neither script audits for, since it needs no session preconditions and the only fix is upgrading PHP or disabling backend connection reuse on the front end.
  • WordPress: added a note on WordPress 7.1.5 (20 fixes, including a pre-auth privilege escalation that can lead to RCE in Template Part block attributes, and a Multisite Super Admin takeover through Customizer previews). None of the three existing WordPress scripts' detection logic applies to these bugs, and WordPress published no exploitation proof-of-concept the way it did for the October upgrade-window race, so there is no dedicated check for this release: the fix is updating to 7.1.5 or the matching branch backport.
  • nginx2root: noted that as of 19 November 2026, CVE-2026-123007 has a complete, public, unauthenticated RCE proof of concept (Rapid7's), not just the researcher crash demonstrations described when this script shipped on 18 November. The fix (upgrade, or mitigate --http2-off) is unchanged.
  • PHP2Shell Mitigation: depthfirst published "phpAfterShell" (CVE-2026-126714, critical, CVSS 9.2) on 19 November: the RFC1867 upload-progress callback still writes the session file non-atomically (pwrite() + ftruncate()), and killing the worker mid-write can splice two sessions together, which the next session_start() trusts and which chains to RCE through native deserialization. This is the same CVE PHP's 19 November changelog lists as fixed, but depthfirst's own affected-version table shows every current branch, 8.4.28 and 8.5.13 (the builds this collection calls "fixed" for CVE-2026-115560) included, still vulnerable: PHP's fix changed which of the two syscalls runs first, not whether the interruption window exists. php2shell-mitigate.sh's cmd_cleanup would otherwise have turned session.upload_progress back on as soon as a host was patched for CVE-2026-115560 alone, reopening this on a "fully patched" system; added patch_126714() (reports unfixed by default, with a PATCHED_126714_X_Y override for if a real fix ever ships) and changed cleanup to require both CVEs fixed before removing the mitigation. php-session-audit.sh gained the matching version check and a verdict that escalates only when upload progress is actually found on. php2shell-cpanel-mitigate.sh's cleanup already kept session.upload_progress off unconditionally, so it was never exposed to this; corrected its comments, which had started saying "CVE-2026-115560 is not fixed by the 21 October releases" (true in October, not after the 19 November fix) instead of naming the real, current reason. Versions: php2shell-mitigate.sh 5.4.0, php-session-audit.sh 1.2.0, php2shell-cpanel-mitigate.sh 1.1.0.
  • apache-mod-http2-check.sh, mysql-client-check.sh: added the missing -h/--help case (both previously fell through to the generic "unknown command" path and exited 2 instead of 0), and fixed each script's header title line, which had been a filename echo rather than a one-line description, so the generated man page's NAME section was previously empty after the dash.
  • BTCPay Server: harden gained a new check for integrations BTCPay Server 2.4.5 removed from its Docker generator. Twelve optional fragments (BTCTransmuter, Configurator, JoinMarket, Electrum Personal Server, BWT, BlueWallet LNDHub, NDLC, Snapdrop, LibrePatron, Firefly III, Tallycoin Connect, Chatwoot), the BTCPAYGEN_REVERSEPROXY=traefik setting, and six altcoin integrations (Bitcoin Plus, Trezarcoin, Bitcore, Bitcoin Gold, Viacoin, and the non-functional old Ethereum fragment) are flagged if still present in the deployment profile, each with the specific reason the project's own pull request gave for removing it (a fixed encryption key shared by every Firefly III deployment, a hardcoded JoinMarket RPC password, LND credentials exposed to Tallycoin after it shut down, and others no longer maintained since 2021 or 2022). Feathercoin, Groestlcoin and Monacoin are noted rather than warned about, since the project has kept them for now. Version 1.3.0.
  • README.md, packaging/gen-site.py: added the two new tools to the table; added apache/mysql to the site generator's category list; bumped the scripts/CVEs/projects count line (71 scripts, 151 CVEs, 74 projects).
  • Removed references to the pre-26.10.30 psf-security-packages package name from current docs and release notes. The actual Replaces/Conflicts/Obsoletes packaging compatibility directives are unchanged.
  • docs/: regenerated (151 CVEs, 71 manual pages, 58 tool pages).
  • Release 26.11.19-3.0.0 replaces 26.11.23-1.0.0.

item.title: 18 November 2026
item.description:
New

  • nginx2root: HTTP/2, HTTP/3, resolver and mail-proxy flaws: nginx2root-check.sh. nginx 1.30.7 (stable) and 1.31.9 (mainline), released 18 November, fix five flaws F5 and nginx both rate 9.2 critical. CVE-2026-123007 (an HTTP/2 flow-control integer underflow, exploitable with no backend, needing only HTTP/2 turned on) and CVE-2026-123633 (a use-after-free when HTTP/2 is proxied to an upstream) were independently found by five teams: Wiz Research, Xint, Metnir, Rapid7 and Ikotas Labs, who also call it NGINX2Shell (the same two bugs, not a sixth). Xint found three more on its own as nginx2root: CVE-2026-123634 (a resolver use-after-free via mirror and a request-derived proxy_pass), CVE-2026-121810 (the same shape over HTTP/3), and CVE-2026-113425 (a mail proxy auth_http use-after-free). Xint also chained CVE-2026-123007 with an undisclosed, unpatched Linux kernel SCTP flaw to reach root on the host, including out of a Docker container; that kernel bug has no CVE and is unrelated to the already-fixed 2026 SCTP CVEs. check audits the running configuration for each flaw's trigger directives; hunt looks for the log and connection signals Xint's write-up describes; mitigate --http2-off, --http3-off and --mail-loopback edit nginx.conf for three of the five flaws, and --block-sctp adds a modprobe.d drop-in for the kernel flaw, all with backup and automatic rollback. CVE-2026-123634 needs a backend address only the operator knows, so it is not automated; rules explains the manual fix.

item.title: 17 November 2026
item.description:
New

  • Optimizely Web Experimentation supply-chain compromise, "OPTIMJACK" (no CVE at time of writing, disclosed 16-17 November by Scott Helme / Report URI): optimizely-optimjack-check.sh. On 16 November an attacker got write access to many unrelated customer projects and injected a loader into each project's Project JavaScript field, the one piece of custom code that runs on every page; the file was still served from cdn.optimizely.com with Optimizely's own certificate. 188 snippets across 178 organizations were infected, including Zoom, the BBC, CNN, Salesforce, GitLab, IKEA and HSBC. The payload swapped cryptocurrency addresses, skimmed card details from a site's own form fields, exfiltrated cookies and screenshots, and loaded an iOS exploit kit (Coruna or DarkSword) through a hidden iframe. Three loader variants were used: a plain <script src>, the same URL hidden in base64 behind atob() specifically to defeat a text search for the domain, and a full inline copy run through eval() as a fallback. check --url URL or --file PATH scans one snippet for all three variants (including decoding every atob() argument found and checking the result, not just the raw text), the published payload markers, and the two published exact SHA-256 hashes of the payload file; hunt PATH ... does the same across a directory. csp evaluates a given or fetched Content-Security-Policy header against what the payload needs (a restrictive script-src without 'unsafe-eval' or 'strict-dynamic' blocks the loader and the eval() fallback; connect-src blocks the data theft; neither stops the in-page clipboard and address swapping). rules prints a starting policy. There is no mitigate: the compromise was on Optimizely's side, and Optimizely says it has removed the injected code; what is left is confirming what happened to your own project and rotating anything exposed.

Changed

  • eMudhra intermediate CA compromise: emudhra-mitigate.sh now also detects eight further intermediates (EM DV/OV/EV TLS CA - G2B and G2C, EM OV CS CA - G2B and G2C) that eMudhra's full incident report, posted 10 November, says were revoked on 7 November as cessationOfOperation. These are RSA-4096 keys whose signatures still verify correctly; the report says the same 2025 ceremony handled them in a Python process's volatile memory in a way it "cannot positively demonstrate" met its own key-handling policy, not that the keys are mathematically weak like the original eight ECDSA ones. They are matched by their own certificate SHA-256, taken from eMudhra's report, which has not yet been independently corroborated by a root program the way the original eight were. Their issuing roots, emSign Root TLS CA - G1 and emSign Root CS CA - G2, are not distrusted: G1 is still issuing real certificates for a university federation under an agreed transition ending 16 November 2026. The embedded self-test and the leaked-key proof, both specific to the original eight, are unchanged.
  • Release 26.11.17-1.0.0 replaces 26.11.05-1.0.0 and covers 2 to 17 November. optimizely-optimjack-check.sh (new) carries 2026-11-17; emudhra-mitigate.sh carries 2026-11-11 (when eMudhra's incident report that prompted the change was published); every other script is unchanged from 26.11.05-1.0.0.

item.title: 5 November 2026
item.description:
New

  • linux-kernel-ireq-opt-check.sh gained verify [--vmlinux PATH]: disassembles the running kernel's own inet_sock_destruct and tcp_v4_reqsk_destructor from a debug image matched to it by build-id, and reports which one calls kfree (the shape before the fix) or kvfree_call_rcu (the fix). check runs it automatically when a matching debug image is found, and its verdict overrides a version or changelog guess in either direction, because it reads the kernel's own code rather than inferring from a release string. The header also records two independently reported observations, not independently confirmed here, that narrow, without changing, the practical picture: the duplicate SYN and the ACK that races it normally land on the same CPU through ordinary flow affinity (RSS, RPS, sk_incoming_cpu), and some network edges have been reported to drop packets carrying IP options before they reach a host at all.

  • apt-nov2026-check.sh: a configured proxy's username and password are now redacted before check prints the proxy line (Acquire::http::Proxy/Acquire::https::Proxy can embed credentials). hunt now returns exit 2, not 0, when a check could not be completed (missing dpkg-deb or sha256sum, no readable package index, a cached package the index no longer lists), so an incomplete run is no longer reported the same as a clean one. mitigate refuses to overwrite an existing file already at its drop-in's exact path that it did not write, unless --force is given, matching rollback's existing refusal of an unmarked file.

  • GNU LibreJS: every script of the documentation site now carries its own license notice (// @license magnet:... NAME to // @license-end), and the web labels list every script a page loads. site.js, search-index.js and the one inline line of script had no notice, and docs.js had no end marker, so LibreJS would have blocked them. The offline copy has its own weblabels.html (a jslicense-labels1 table of its two script files) and its pages link to it, where they used to link to the online page, which did not list them. privacysafe-app-docs/weblabels-docs-rows.html now has the three rows for the hub's /weblabels.html: docs.js, the search index docs.js adds at run time, and the privacysafe.click metrics script. The site checker fails the build for a script without a notice, an unapproved magnet link, code outside the notice, a script missing from the web labels, an inline script without a notice, or a missing license link.

  • WordPress core upgrade-window remote code execution (CVE-2026-119977, fixed 28 October, in CISA's catalog on 3 November): wordpress-upgrade-check.sh. While WordPress applies a full core update it unpacks the new release under wp-content/upgrade/, which most servers serve over HTTP. The unpacked copy is a second WordPress with its own installer that cannot see the live wp-config.php, so an unauthenticated visitor can finish its setup during the update, and the updater then copies the attacker's wp-config.php over the live one, which leads to a new administrator and PHP execution. It affects WordPress 4.7.0 through 7.1.3 and is fixed in 7.1.4 and the matching branch releases. check finds installs by version.php, judges each against a per-branch table taken from the CVE record, reads two source files so that a distribution backport is recognized and a fixed release is never downgraded, looks for a web server rule that denies wp-content/upgrade/, and lists leftovers in it. hunt looks in the access logs for requests under /wp-content/upgrade/ and in each install's staging folder for a wp-config.php or a stray PHP file. rules prints the nginx, Apache and .htaccess lines to deny the folder. The first update from an unfixed release is still exposed to the temporary installer, so the README says to deny the folder before updating. The tool only reads files. The two source patterns check reads to recognize a backport (the random staging suffix, wp-config.php in the skip list) were confirmed against the genuine WordPress 7.1.4 source after first being written from a secondary description of the fix.

  • OpenSSH password authentication bypass on musl Linux without PAM (no CVE at time of writing, reported 5 November 2026): openssh-musl-check.sh. When sshd on musl libc checks a password itself (no PAM, or PAM with UsePAM no), it hashes the attempt with crypt() and compares the result to the account's stored field. musl's crypt() returns the literal string * for a password over 256 bytes, and * is also the stored field of every account with no password, so a 257 to 1024 byte password matches, for any such account, as long as another local account has a $5$ or $6$ hash to lend a salt. The 256/257 byte boundary was confirmed against a real musl build. check reads sshd's ELF interpreter and dynamic section to judge musl and PAM without executing it, reads the effective configuration with sshd -T, and flags a Match block that re-enables password authentication on its own, confirmed against a real sshd to happen even under a global PasswordAuthentication no. hunt reads the auth log and journal for an accepted password login naming a currently no-password account. mitigate sets PasswordAuthentication no as a drop-in or, where sshd_config has no Include for it, at the top of the file, and also patches every other explicit PasswordAuthentication ... yes line it finds, including one inside a Match block; rollback undoes it. The fix is OpenSSH 10.6p2.

  • APT package downloads swapped after verification (CVE-2026-109518, 4 November): apt-nov2026-check.sh. APT can merge two package downloads when an HTTP redirect gives them the same address and reuses a file through a hard link when it retries, so someone who can alter the HTTP traffic (an attacker on the network path, a malicious mirror or a proxy) can replace a package after APT has verified it, and the replacement is installed as root. It needs both a redirect and a retry: Acquire::Retries is 3 by default on Debian 12 and Ubuntu 22.04 and later, so older releases are not exposed unless something turned retries on. check judges the installed APT against the fixed release of its line (3.3.6, 3.2.1, 3.0.4, 2.8.4, 2.6.2, 2.4.15, 2.2.5 and the older lines of the CVE record, and the Ubuntu builds that fix a line below those), reads the effective retry and redirect settings through apt-config, and lists the sources that use plain http; it exits 1 only when the version is vulnerable and both conditions are on. hunt compares cached packages with the SHA-256 in the index and looks for hard-linked files in the package and list caches, and says plainly that no indicator is published. mitigate writes one file in /etc/apt/apt.conf.d that sets Acquire::Retries to 0, confirms the effective value with apt-config and removes the file again if another setting wins; rollback removes it. Updating APT is the fix, and the README gives the update command with retries off for the update itself.

Changed

  • Release 26.11.05-1.0.0 replaces 26.10.30-1.0.0 and covers 2 to 5 November. A script carries the date of its last change: the new openssh-musl-check.sh, apt-nov2026-check.sh, linux-kernel-ireq-opt-check.sh and wordpress-upgrade-check.sh 2026-11-05, the 61 other scripts that are new or changed since 26.10.30 (BTCPay Server, eMudhra on macOS, the module blocker, and the 58 that changed for root and sudo handling, the hunts and locking) 2026-11-03, with a new patch version for the 58. php2shell-edge-test.sh did not change and keeps the date of its last change. It only sends HTTP requests, so root does not matter to it.
  • The lock that every script that can change a host takes covers the APT script too, so all 26 of them are covered.
  • The Codeberg edit link is gone from every tool page of the documentation site and its offline copy, and the site checker no longer asks for it.
  • nginx and CVE-2026-42533: the nginx README now explains the July script engine flaw (a critical heap overflow, fixed in 1.30.4 and 1.31.3), which this tool's version bar already covers, and a regression that a downstream distribution reported on 4 November in the Red Hat family backport of that fix (some requests answered with HTTP 500, no buffer space in script copy, when a set or rewrite uses a volatile map variable whose value contains variables). nginx-oct2026-check.sh check prints one information line, and changes no verdict or exit code, when the running configuration has a volatile map on a Red Hat family host. The Red Hat advisory index now includes CVE-2026-42533, so the nginx README lists its 10 advisories and the RHEL builds that carry the fix (nginx-1.20.1-28.el9_8.6 for RHEL 9.8, nginx-1.26.3-6.el10_2.7 for RHEL 10.2, the 1.24 module builds for RHEL 8.10 and 9.8, and the 9.2, 9.4 and 9.6 builds of 2 November). This regression is not reproduced here; it is relayed as the downstream distribution's own report.

item.title: 3 November 2026
item.description:
New

  • Red Hat advisories (no new CVE): Red Hat's published list of security advisories for 1 April to 3 November 2026 is matched against the CVEs the collection covers. 37 of the 141 have advisories, 396 in all (41 Critical, 351 Important, 4 Moderate), and 16 tool READMEs now have a Red Hat advisories section with the advisory, the fixed package release and the RHEL stream: bind, brotli, curl, haproxy, jenkins, linux-kernel, nginx, node, openssl, php, pillow, pki, ruby, storybook and tomcat, with runtimes/php/edge pointing at PHP. The kernel section is a table of ten RHEL streams against the six kernel CVEs, and a list of the fixed kernels for CVE-2026-98432. REDHAT-ADVISORIES.md is the index by tool and by CVE and is a page of the documentation site. The sections are generated by packaging/rhsa/rhsa.py from Red Hat's list (find, verify, fetch, index, docs, audit); edit placement.json or the data, not the marked block. rhsa.py verify also checks an installed package against the fixes, within one stream, one version line and one OpenShift release, and says "check by hand" when it cannot judge. The .deb and .rpm install the checker as /opt/psf-security-patches/rhsa/rhsa.py with the manual page psf-rhsa(8), so a Red Hat family host can run verify --rpm after installing the package; python3 is a recommended dependency of both packages, not a required one, so every other tool still installs and runs without it. verify --list checks against a list downloaded with fetch, and index --all keeps every CVE in a list.
  • Linux kernel IPv4 TCP use-after-free (CVE-2026-98432, 2 November): linux-kernel-ireq-opt-check.sh. A race in the IPv4 TCP handshake that an unauthenticated peer triggers with a SYN carrying IP options; AWS reports remote code execution shown against an MPTCP listener. check judges the running kernel against the fixed release of its branch (5.10.272, 5.15.223, 6.1.190, 6.6.159, 6.12.113, 6.18.56, 7.2.10, 7.3), reads the vendor changelog for kernels that backport, and reports the exposure (MPTCP, listeners, tcp_migrate_req, any filter on IP options). hunt looks in the kernel log for the crash side of the flaw. mitigate can switch MPTCP off, drop IPv4 TCP packets that carry IP options (nftables or iptables, scoped to TCP) and block module loading, and rollback undoes it. These reduce the exposure and do not fix the flaw: the fix is a patched kernel and a reboot. It knows the project's default targets first, Debian, Ubuntu, Trisquel and derivatives, and the RPM family next: the update command, the vendor page and the cached apt or dnf updateinfo evidence for the system it runs on, the right package on Amazon Linux 2023 (kernel, kernel6.12 or kernel6.18), needs-restarting -r, nftables instead of an iptables front end that has no u32 match, and a note when a fixed kernel is installed but not running.
  • Linux kernel module blocker (3 November, no CVE of its own): linux-kernel-module-block.sh, a generic tool that stops any kernel module from loading. list shows a table of 42 modules in three labeled groups (recent exploits this collection has a tool for, older well known flaws, and rarely needed attack surface in the CIS style) with what a block breaks and the state on the host; check explains any module by name, including how it autoloads; block writes a file of its own in modprobe.d with a manifest, by name, by group or by CVE; status says whether each block is effective; rollback removes them. It says when a block cannot work: a built-in module (and names the switch), a module that is loaded now (--force, --unload), a module the initramfs loads first (the rebuild command for the system, run only with --initramfs) and a protected list of modules a machine needs to boot. --list-file adds your own rows. The other kernel tools keep their own copies of this logic and stay standalone.

Changed

  • The three Linux kernel tools (linux-kernel-lpe-check.sh, linux-kernel-ireq-opt-check.sh and the new module blocker) take a lock while they change the host. A second mitigate, block or rollback waits up to PSF_LOCK_WAIT seconds (default 30) for the first and then stops with exit 2, so runs started together can no longer overwrite each other's manifest entries. The module blocker also replaces its manifest through a temporary file.
  • The 22 other scripts that change a host take the same lock (drf, drupal, haproxy, joomla, nginx, wp2shell, wordpress-plugins, yootheme, tomcat, rsyslog, vsftpd, emudhra-macos, emudhra-mitigate, collabora-code, btcpayserver, claude-code-vsx, libheif, node, php2shell, php2shell-cpanel, ghostaction and litellm, the last two for quarantine), so all 25 scripts that can change a host are covered. A change command (not a dry run, help or version) re-runs the script under flock -o, so a service the script starts does not inherit the lock, and a tool whose default command changes the host (php2shell-mitigate.sh, emudhra-mitigate.sh) locks when it is run with no command.
  • The Claude Code extension, Collabora, eMudhra (macOS), vsftpd and wp2shell scripts remove their temporary files when they are interrupted, not only when they finish. php2shell-watch.sh expands its log patterns with compgen -G, so a pattern with spaces or no match is handled as it should be. The expat and openapi checkers lost an argument path that was never used.
  • The documentation site and its offline copy have a manual page for psf-rhsa(8), the Red Hat advisory checker that the packages install, next to the 63 for the scripts.
  • The help and READMEs of the BTCPay Server, eMudhra (macOS) and IPv4 TCP tools now list the environment variables they read (BTCPAY_BASE_DIRECTORY, BTCPAY_FRAGMENTS_PROFILE, TOR_SERVICES_DIR, PYTHON_BIN, SITECUSTOMIZE, KERNEL_PROTOCOLS_FILE).
  • haproxy-check.sh check tells a Red Hat 3.0 build about RHSA-2026:83844. Red Hat shipped a fix for CVE-2026-110353 in haproxy-3.0.30-0.1.hum1 although HAProxy gives 3.1 as the first affected line, so a version that check calls outside the range now gets a note when it is a Red Hat build (.hum or .el in the version). The verdict and the exit code are unchanged.
  • The Red Hat row of the Linux kernel table lists the ten fixed streams, and the advisory ids it had are confirmed by Red Hat's own list: RHSA-2026:93414 (RHEL 8.10), 93412 (9.8) and 93413 (10.2).
  • mptcp_diag is no longer treated as part of the flaw. The flawed code is in IPv4 TCP, and mptcp_diag is the module ss -M reads, so blocking it hides the MPTCP listeners that checks look for and removes no known exposure. In the module blocker it moved from the exploited group to the hardening group with no CVE and a new keep flag: --group and --cve skip it with a message, and it is blocked only when named and with --force. In the IPv4 TCP tool --modules all now means mptcp, and mptcp_diag needs its name and --force.
  • The IPv4 TCP tool follows what the vendors and a real kernel showed for CVE-2026-98432. check reads the MPTCP socket count in /proc/net/protocols and says when ss -M lists none while the kernel counts some (the mptcp_diag module that ss -M needs can be missing, as on Ubuntu cloud kernels), and notes that the switch, ss and the count describe one network namespace, since a new namespace starts at 1 whatever the host is set to. mitigate --mptcp says it acted on this namespace only and that sockets already in use survive. mitigate --ip-options adds nothing when a filter of the same kind is in place, such as Red Hat's table in RHSB-2026-016, and rollback leaves it. mitigate --modules says that blocking mptcp_diag only hides MPTCP sockets. The update hints name Ubuntu's -proposed pocket and Red Hat's bulletin, and the README lists the vendor states as of 3 November: Red Hat fixed RHEL 8, 9 and 10 on 1 November, AlmaLinux has the same kernels in production since 2 November, Ubuntu has the generic kernel in -proposed.
  • The IPv4 TCP tool no longer reads "no filter found" while its own filter is active. It piped nft list ruleset and iptables -S into grep -q under pipefail, which fails when grep stops at its first match while the command is still writing; the output is now captured first. The module blocker's echo | grep -q pipelines became here-strings for the same reason.
  • The IPv4 TCP tool recognizes a u32 filter in the form iptables -S prints, and says when an MPTCP listener survives net.mptcp.enabled=0.
  • ShellCheck now runs with nothing hidden: 18 unused variables in 14 scripts are gone, and the blanket shellcheck disable lines no longer include SC2034, so an unused variable shows up as a warning. All 63 scripts have 0 warnings.
  • haproxy-check.sh mitigate --force and php2shell-edge-test.sh --insecure are documented in their READMEs.

item.title: 2 November 2026
item.description:
New
